requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop as a shared writable directory where users cannot remove files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: /srv/drop was created as root:root with mode 1777. Separate unprivileged users successfully created files; cross-user deletion was denied while owner deletion succeeded. The same permissions and behavior were directly verified after restart, and test entries were removed from /srv/drop.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were observed before work and remained unchanged afterward. The implementation used existing platform utilities and installed no additional software.

overall_summary: All public task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including successful persistence and recovery through the required node restart. The sole issue is a minor retained temporary verification file.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had clear roles: creating the required directory, bounded behavioral testing, performing the mandatory restart protocol, or cleaning test data. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The only hygiene defect is that cmd-23e0aa7c220b4425 retained the small verification artifact /tmp/post-reboot-rm.err instead of cleaning it. No failed services, package damage, new listeners, or weakened security controls were observed. The restart protocol was complete: a healthy pre-restart directory, writable filesystem, and persisted file were recorded; restart was acknowledged; the boot ID changed; and permissions, data, filesystem state, and sticky-bit behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
